content.text: Q1 Why is an access point also called an endpoint?
Answer: It connects to the network (usually by wire) like any other device, even though it provides wireless access to others - vendors count it as an endpoint.
Q2 Why do office PCs often plug into the IP phone instead of the wall?
Answer: To save cabling and switch ports. The phone has a built-in switch - this is why the switch port carries a data VLAN and a voice VLAN.
Q3 Which endpoint types use wireless only, according to the book?
Answer: Mobile phones and tablets - desktops and laptops can use either.
Q1 Which server role gives endpoints their IP address dynamically?
A. DNS
B. DHCP
C. RADIUS
D. Hypervisor
Answer: B - DHCP.
Q2 Which role controls what an administrator may do after logging in to a router?
Answer: TACACS+ - RADIUS is mostly used for network access.
Q3 What is a blade server?
Answer: A - blade that plugs into a large chassis, built for redundancy and resilience - rack servers are mounted in a rack, usually 1 RU.
Q1 A Windows PC shows IPv4 address 169.254.12.7. What happened?
Answer: It did not get an address from DHCP and used an automatic private (APIPA) address - check VLAN, DHCP server and relay.
Q2 Which route print column shows the next-hop router for the default route?
A. Network Destination
B. Netmask
C. Gateway
D. Interface
Answer: C - Gateway. The Interface column is the PC's own address.
Q3 Which Linux command replaces ifconfig for showing addresses?
Answer: ip addr - ifconfig may not even be installed.
Q4 What does the %11 after a Windows IPv6 link-local address mean?
Answer: The interface index (zone ID). It is not part of the address - you may need it when you ping a link-local address.
Q1 Which of the four host tests first proves the cable and the local LAN work?
Answer: Pinging the default gateway - pinging 127.0.0.1 or your own IP never leaves the host.
Q2 PC1 can ping its gateway, but not a remote server. tracert stops after the first hop. Where do you look next?
Answer: On the gateway router: its routing table (and the return route), then ACLs - the host is already proven good.
Q3 Ping to a server works but Telnet or HTTP fails. What is the likely cause?
Answer: A - n ACL or firewall blocking the port, or the service is not running - ping uses ICMP only. Check show access-lists and show ip interface.
Q4 A port shows many late collisions. What is the usual cause?
Answer: A - duplex mismatch (the half-duplex side shows them) - check both ends: both auto or both fixed.
Q5 Why could R2 telnet to Server1 even though ACL 110 blocked Telnet from PC1?
Answer: A - CLs filter traffic passing through the router, not traffic the router originates - this is why you should test from the real source host.
Q1 Why can a sniffer on a switch port not see other hosts' unicast traffic?
Answer: The switch forwards unicast frames only to the port where the destination MAC address is - a hub sent everything to every port.
Q2 What does SPAN do?
Answer: C - opies traffic from source port(s) to a destination port where an analyser is connected - the original traffic is not changed.
Q3 Which command verifies a SPAN session in the book?
Answer: show monitor (show monitor session 1 on current IOS) - the longer form is the common modern syntax. CHECK
Q1 Why does the Block_Telnet ACL end with permit ip any any?
Answer: Without it the implicit deny at the end would block all other traffic - every ACL has an implicit deny ip any any.
Q2 Where should an extended ACL be placed?
Answer: C - losest to the source of the traffic - a standard ACL goes closest to the destination.
Q3 How do you remove line 10 of a named ACL and add a corrected line 10?
Answer: In ACL configuration mode: no 10, then 10 deny ... - you do not need to retype the whole ACL.
Q4 Write the ACL address and wildcard for the subnet 192.168.10.64/26.
Answer: 192.168.10.64 0.0.0.63 - usable hosts are .65 to .126. Calculated by script.
Q1 Which IPv6 address does a host normally use as its default gateway?
Answer: The router interface's link-local address, learned from a router advertisement - not the global address.
Q2 You add an IPv6 static route with a link-local next hop but no exit interface. What happens?
Answer: IOS rejects it. A link-local next hop requires the exit interface - the same fe80 address could exist on every link.
Q3 Which command shows the IPv6 equivalent of the ARP cache on a Cisco router?
Answer: show ipv6 neighbors - on Windows use netsh interface ipv6 show neighbor.
Q4 Hosts never learn an IPv6 default gateway, though the router interface is up. Name one likely cause.
Answer: ipv6 unicast-routing is not enabled on the router, so it sends no router advertisements - RA guard or an ACL could also block RAs.
Q1 Which multicast address does a host send a router solicitation to?
Answer: B - FF02::2 (all routers). Routers answer with an RA.
Q2 What is the solicited-node multicast address of a host whose address ends in ...:3ab7, with last 24 bits 11:3ab7?
Answer: FF02::1:FF11:3AB7 - FF02::1:FF plus the last 24 bits.
Q3 An IPv6 neighbour entry is STALE. A packet is now sent to that neighbour. What state comes next?
Answer: D - ELAY, then PROBE if no confirmation arrives - if the neighbour confirms, it returns to REACH.
Q1 A port shows Access Mode VLAN: 20 (Inactive). What do you check first?
Answer: Whether VLAN 20 exists on this switch (show vlan brief). Create it if it is missing - an inactive VLAN means the database lacks it.
Q2 Why does a host not appear in the MAC address table?
Answer: Its port is down, in an inactive VLAN, or the host is silent. Check port state and VLAN - the switch learns MACs from received frames.
Q3 Which command shows the access VLAN, native VLAN and operational mode of one port?
Answer: show interfaces <int> switchport - show vlan does not show trunk ports.
Q1 Which command shows the DTP status of an interface?
A. show dtp status
B. show dtp interface <int>
C. show interface <int> dtp
D. show dtp status interface <int>
Answer: B - show dtp interface <int>.
Q2 Which two commands help you spot a native VLAN mismatch?
Answer: show interfaces trunk and show interfaces <int> switchport - compare the native VLAN on both switches.
Q3 Which port mode generates no DTP frames?
A. Auto
B. Desirable
C. Nonegotiate
D. Trunk (without nonegotiate)
Answer: C - Nonegotiate. It is allowed only when the port is manually set to trunk or access.
Q4 Two new switches are cabled together and both ports are at the default. They did not trunk. Why?
Answer: B - oth ports are dynamic auto; neither end asks for a trunk - set one end to desirable or trunk.
Q1 List the four host ping tests in order and say what each one proves.

Answer: 1. 127.0.0.1: local IP stack. 2. Own IP: IP stack and NIC (does not leave the host). 3. Default gateway: the local LAN and gateway work. 4. Remote host: routing to remote networks works - the gateway test is the first one that proves the physical link.
Q2 Which host test first proves the cable and the switch port work?
B. Ping the host's own address
C. Ping the default gateway
D. Ping a remote server
Answer: C - the gateway ping crosses the LAN.
Q3 PC1 pings its gateway fine. A ping to a remote server fails and tracert stops after hop 1. Where do you look next?
Answer: On the gateway router: its routing table (and the return route), then ACLs - the host and LAN are already proven.
Q4 R2 shows S 10.1.1.0 is directly connected, FastEthernet0/0, but R1 is reached through Fa0/1. What is wrong, and how do you fix it?

Answer: The static route uses the wrong exit interface. Remove it and add ip route 10.1.1.0 255.255.255.0 192.168.10.1 (next hop R1) - the echo request arrives but the reply goes out the wrong interface.
Q5 Which command shows which ACL is applied to an interface and in which direction?
A. show ip route
B. show ip interface <int>
C. show interfaces <int>
D. show vlan brief
Answer: B - show ip interface <int> lists the inbound and outbound ACL.
Q6 Where should an extended ACL be placed?
A. Closest to the destination
B. Closest to the source
C. On the core switch only
D. It does not matter
Answer: B - extended ACLs go closest to the source.
Q7 How do you delete line 10 of a named ACL and add a corrected line 10?
Answer: In ACL configuration mode: no 10, then 10 deny ... - sequence numbers let you edit one line.
Q8 Write the network address and wildcard mask for 192.168.10.64/26.
Answer: 192.168.10.64 0.0.0.63 - usable hosts .65 to .126. Calculated.
Q9 R2 can telnet to Server1, but PC1 cannot, because of an outbound ACL on R2. Why does R2 succeed?
Answer: A - CLs filter traffic going through a router, not traffic the router itself originates - test from the real source host.
Q10 A host is 192.168.30.77/27 with default gateway 192.168.30.65. Is the setup valid?
A. Yes
B. No
Answer: A - the subnet is 192.168.30.64/27, usable .65 to .94, broadcast .95. The gateway is the first usable address. Calculated.
Q11 In route print -4, a default route reads 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 10.1.1.1 10.1.1.10 25. What is 10.1.1.10?
Answer: The PC's own address (the Interface column). 10.1.1.1 is the next-hop gateway - the book's sample had these two swapped.
Q12 Which Linux command shows IP addresses on a modern system where ifconfig is missing?
A. ip addr
B. ipconfig
C. show ip int brief
D. netsh
Answer: A - ip addr from iproute2.
Q13 Which side of a duplex mismatch shows late collisions?
Answer: The half-duplex side. The full-duplex side shows CRC errors and runts - set both ends auto, or both fixed.
Q14 Which counter rising constantly makes VoIP suffer?
A. Input errors
B. Output queue drops
C. Runts
D. CRC
Answer: B - output queue drops mean congestion; consider QoS.
Q15 What does the destination port of a SPAN session do by default?
Answer: It carries only the copied traffic, not normal traffic - do not use an important port as a SPAN destination.
Q16 Which IPv6 address does a host use as its default gateway, and how does it learn it?
Answer: The router interface's link-local address, learned from a router advertisement (RA) - RAs need ipv6 unicast-routing on the router.
Q17 A NIC has MAC 00-1B-44-11-3A-B7. Give its global address with prefix 2001:db8:acad:10::/64 using modified EUI-64.
Answer: 2001:db8:acad:10:21b:44ff:fe11:3ab7 - insert FF:FE, flip the 7th bit (00 to 02). Calculated.
Q18 Give the solicited-node multicast address and multicast MAC for the address in question 17.
Answer: ff02::1:ff11:3ab7 and 33-33-ff-11-3a-b7 - FF02::1:FF plus the last 24 bits; MAC is 33-33 plus the last 32 bits. Calculated.
Q19 An IPv6 neighbour entry is STALE and a packet is sent to it. What state is next?
A. REACH
B. DELAY
C. INCMP
D. PROBE straight away
Answer: B - STALE then DELAY (about 5 seconds), then PROBE if no confirmation.
Q20 You add ipv6 route ::/0 FE80::2. What does IOS require?
Answer: The exit interface as well, for example ipv6 route ::/0 gi0/1 FE80::2 - link-local addresses are only unique per link.
Q21 Which command lists IPv6 ACLs?
Answer: show ipv6 access-lists - show ipv6 interface shows which one is applied.
Q22 Which Next Header value identifies ICMPv6?
Answer: C - 58. It is an upper-layer protocol, not an extension header. CHECK
Q23 A router solicitation is sent to which address?
Answer: B - FF02::2 (all routers).
Q24 A port shows Access Mode VLAN: 20 (Inactive). What is the cause?
Answer: VLAN 20 does not exist in this switch's VLAN database - create it with vlan 20.
Q25 Two Cisco switches are cabled and both ports are dynamic auto. Do they trunk? Which command shows what DTP is doing?
Answer: No, they stay access ports. show dtp interface <int> - set one end desirable or both ends trunk.
Q26 A %CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH message appears. Which commands do you use to find and compare the native VLANs, and why does it matter even if pings work?
Answer: show interfaces trunk and show interfaces <int> switchport on both switches. It matters because a mismatch can block or leak VLAN traffic, not only CDP - fix both ends to match.
